title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VI of the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes builds an axiomatic, point-free theory of 'figures'. An 'atelier' is a set F of figures with two relations: ≤ (inclusion of figures) and ≪ (a 'well inside' or relatively-compact-type relation), subject to axioms At1–At7. M ⊂ F is the set of irreducible ('elementary') figures. On p.37 Grothendieck defined morphisms of ateliers and tried to define sub-ateliers by requiring the inclusion to be a morphism, i.e. stability under certain Sups and intersections. He then asked whether it would be more reasonable to require closure under sub-figures. This page opens by saying the earlier conditions were inadequate: stability inside Fig(L) does not pass to sub-figures, and Sup_≤ stability was being demanded only in conjunction with ≪.

New definition ('Je reprends les définitions'). Let (F, ≤, ≪) satisfy At1–At7.
- A sub-atelier is a non-empty subset F' ⊂ F that is closed downward for ≤: every sub-figure of a figure in F' lies in F'. An inserted phrase adds 'and stable under non-empty Sups existing in F''.
- F' is moreover 'spécieux/spacieux' if it is stable under arbitrary Sups that exist in F (non-empty ones).
- A margin note says non-emptiness is equivalent to the smallest element ∅_F lying in F'.
- These notions depend only on ≤, but F' is given the induced ≤ and ≪.

Claim. With M' = F' ∩ M, the elements of M' are exactly the (strictly) irreducible elements of F' for ≤. The reference given is to Ch. IV, p.53.

Proof (after several false starts were struck out). For X ∈ F', the families (F_i) majorized by X are the same in F and in F', because F' is downward closed. The inclusion F' → F commutes with Sup, so 'X = Sup F_i' means the same in F' as in F. Hence 'for every such family X = Sup F_i implies X = F_i for some i' holds in F' iff it holds in F.

The page breaks off at 'Dans le cas d'un spécieux, on récupère…'. On p.39 the definition is recast purely order-theoretically: a poset with bounded Sups and a least element, closed parts, 'ample' versus 'spacieuse'. There Grothendieck notes that a lower set automatically inherits bounded sups that agree with those of F.

In modern terms: for a down-set (order ideal) of a poset with bounded joins, completely join-irreducible elements are intrinsic to the principal ideal ↓X, so irreducibility is inherited both ways. This is a routine lattice-theoretic lemma serving the construction of sub-objects in his axiomatic topology of figures.
errors: No mathematical error in the final argument. The added clause 'stable par Sup non-vides dans F'' is redundant: for a down-closed F', a family majorized in F' has its F-sup ≤ the bound, hence in F'. Grothendieck himself observes this on p.39.
Struck-out passages show an initial muddle: an 'X ∈ M' versus 'X ∈ F'' slip, and an attempted two-direction proof. These were replaced by the cleaner 'same families, same sups' argument.
The opening sentence is fragmentary, and its claim (that stability within Fig(L) does not pass to sub-figures) is stated without proof.

ideas.what: Sub-atelier defined as a non-empty down-closed subset (order ideal) with induced relations; 'spacious' if also closed under all existing sups of the ambient structure
ideas.modern_name: lower set / order ideal; join-closed (sup-closed) down-set, cf. 'downward closed and directed-sup closed' (Scott-closed sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard order theory (Birkhoff; Scott 1970s for Scott-closed sets)

ideas.what: Irreducible elements of a down-closed sub-poset are exactly the irreducibles of the ambient poset lying in it
ideas.modern_name: completely join-irreducible elements are determined by the principal ideal ↓x

ideas.what: Axiomatic point-free framework of 'ateliers' (figures with inclusion ≤ and a 'well inside' relation ≪, irreducible figures M), as part of a tame-topology 'analysis situs'
ideas.modern_name: point-free topology / continuous posets with way-below relation; o-minimal-style tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Scott, Gierz–Hofmann–Keimel et al. (continuous lattices, 1980); van den Dries (o-minimality); locale theory (Isbell, Johnstone)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is advocated programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the atelier axiomatics itself appears unpublished

missed.claim: This page is a small piece of an unpublished 1986 axiomatization ('ateliers', At1–At7) of spaces of figures by two order-type relations ≤ and ≪, with irreducible figures playing the role of points. That axiomatic program is not in the literature. Its relation to continuous posets and domain theory, and to the tame-topology program of the Esquisse, has not been documented. The content of this specific page, however, is routine order theory.
missed.quote: Soit (F, ≪) un atelier At1 - At7 ... Un sous-atelier est une partie non vide F' de F, fermée par ≤
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historians and specialists of tame topology or point-free topology might want to compare Grothendieck's axioms with continuous lattices, proximity/strong-inclusion locales and o-minimal structures. That requires reading the surrounding pages, not this one alone.

deep.surprise_reason: The page reformulates a definition and proves a standard lattice-theoretic lemma (irreducibility is inherited by order ideals). Only the larger unpublished 'atelier' framework is of interest, and nothing on this page itself is new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'des conditions : F stable dans Fig(L) ne passe pas à une sous-figure, et par Sup≤ (car demandé dans conjonction avec ≪)' rather than 'stable par Fig(L) [?]'.
'(on verra plus loin les raisons ultérieures pour ...)' seems to end with 'ce saut' / 'ceci'; uncertain.
In the spacious definition, '(si non vides, supposés exister dans F')' should probably read 'dans F'; p.39 defines spacieuse as stable under majorized Sups in F.
'cf. §? IV, p. 53' is probably 'cf. Ch. IV, p. 53'.
Margin reads 'non vide : équivaut à φ_F ∈ F'' (φ_F denotes the least element ∅_F), consistent with p.39.
